newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Private sector industrial output grows by 1.9 percent during first half of 1996 despite drought-related power cuts that affected business and industry, the Central Bank says.
$12 million World Bank funded industrial waste water treatment plant for Colombo soon.
Government lifts four-month ban on transportation of medicines to Mallavi, a northern village which has become a temporary home to thousands of minority Tamil refugees.
Armed forces in the east placed on alert after sighting of suspected rebel arms ship off the eastern coast.
Sri Lanka Muslim Congress (SLMC) opposes budget proposal to set up casinos in five-star hotels. SLMC is a partner in the ruling People's Alliance government headed by President Chandrika Kumaratunga.
Sri Lankan Buddhists urged to contribute to restore Buddhagaya, the venerated 1500-year old Buddhist shrine in Bihar, India, which is in a state of decay.
More than 8,000 Sri Lankans are HIV infected, health authorities say.
Local government elections, postponed three times by the government, to be held before April next year, government sources say.
Moderate Tamil political leaders urge parliament to appoint commission to look into alleged sexual harrassment of Tamil civilians in the northern Jaffna peninsula.
Tamil refugees of war confined to camps now face serious food and health problems, moderate Tamil member of parliament Neelan Tiruchelvam says.
